subject: physics
title: Required practical: force and extension of a spring
key_idea: Hang weights on a spring, measure how far it stretches, and plot force against extension. The line is straight up to the limit of proportionality, and its gradient gives the spring constant. The work done is ½ke².

blocks.text: The investigation measures the extension of a spring for different forces. This section covers the apparatus and the steps.

items.meaning: The force on the spring, from the weights added.

items.text: Clamp a stand to the bench. Hang the spring from a clamp.
Use a second clamp and boss to hold a metre ruler vertically alongside the spring.
Read the ruler level with the bottom of the spring, with no weight on it.
Hang a 2 N weight from the bottom of the spring and record the new position of the bottom of the spring.
Add more weights so that the force increases by 2 N each time, up to 10 N. Record the length each time.

items: Change the force by adding weights. Measure the length each time.
Extension = new length − original length.
Fix the ruler vertically so the readings are accurate.

blocks.text: Plot force on the vertical axis and extension on the horizontal axis. The shape of the graph tells you if the spring obeys Hooke's law.

items: A straight line through the origin shows force is directly proportional to extension.
If the line curves at higher forces, the spring has passed its limit of proportionality.
In the straight part, the spring constant is force divided by extension.
The work done in stretching, up to the limit of proportionality, is the energy stored in the spring.

where: k is the spring constant in newtons per metre (N/m).

diagram.alt: Calculate the spring constant from a force and the length of the spring. New numbers each time.
diagram.question: A spring has an original length of 12.0 cm. A force of {F} N makes its length {L} cm. Calculate the spring constant.
working: Extension = {L} − 12 cm, then ÷ 100 to give metres

diagram.alt: Choose a spring and a mass to hang from it, and see the force, extension and energy stored.

items: Plot force against extension. The gradient of the straight part is k.
Convert extension to metres before using k = F ÷ e.
The line curves beyond the limit of proportionality.

blocks.text: Marks are given for noticing what makes the data inaccurate and how to fix it, and for managing risks.

items: Holding the ruler by hand, or not clamping it vertical, gives errors.
Misjudging the position of the bottom of the spring, or parallax error, gives errors.
Fix the ruler close to the spring and make sure it is vertical.
Attach a pointer to the bottom of the spring.
Use a ruler with a better resolution, such as millimetre divisions.
Use a greater range of forces, and use more weights in smaller steps.
Find the limit of proportionality.
Repeat the readings, discard anomalous results and calculate a mean.
The stand could tip over, or masses could fall off, and hurt the student. Clamp the base of the stand to the desk, or do the investigation on the floor.
The spring could snap and hurt the student. Wear goggles and limit the mass hung on the spring.
Use a clamped vertical ruler, a pointer and a fine scale to improve accuracy.
Use a greater range of forces and repeat to calculate a mean.
Clamp the stand, keep masses low and wear goggles.

checks.q: Describe how to find the extension of a spring when a weight is added.
checks.a: Measure the original length and the extended length of the spring with a ruler. Extension = extended length − original length.

checks.q: A force of 4.0 N gives a spring an extension of 0.064 m. Calculate the spring constant.
Give one risk of harm in this investigation and a precaution to reduce it.
checks.a: The stand could tip over or masses could fall and hurt the student, so clamp the base of the stand to the desk. Or the spring could snap, so wear goggles.

exam_phrases: set up a clamp stand with a clamp and hang the spring from it
fix a metre ruler alongside the spring
record the position of the bottom of the spring
attach a pointer to the bottom of the spring
clamp base of stand to desk
use a greater range of forces

mistakes.wrong: To improve the accuracy of the results, repeat the measurements.
mistakes.right: Repeating the measurements is not enough for a cause of inaccuracy. Say what is inaccurate, such as the ruler not clamped vertical or misjudging the position of the bottom of the spring, or parallax error.

mistakes.wrong: Do the investigation on a table so the weights are easy to reach.
mistakes.right: Do it on the laboratory floor, because masses could fall off the spring and cause injury or damage if done on a table.

mistakes.wrong: The extension of the spring is the length of the spring with the weight on.
mistakes.right: Extension = extended length – original length, so measure both lengths.

worked_example.question: A student carried out an investigation to determine the spring constant of a spring. The data obtained: force 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 N with extension 0.0, 3.5, 8.0, 12.5, 16.0, 20.0 cm. Describe a method the student could have used to obtain the data. Your answer should include any cause of inaccuracy in the data. Your answer may include a labelled diagram.
answer_points: Set up a clamp stand with a clamp and hang the spring from the clamp.
Use a second clamp and boss to fix a (half) metre ruler alongside the spring.
Record the ruler reading level with the bottom of the spring.
Hang a 2 N weight from the spring and record the new position of the bottom of the spring.
Calculate the extension of the spring.
Add further weights so that the force increases 2 N at a time up to 10 N, recording the position and calculating the extension each time.
Cause of inaccuracy: the ruler not fixed in position or not vertical, misjudging the position of the bottom of the spring, or parallax error.
worked_example.tip: Level-marked. Give the steps in a logical order and include a cause of inaccuracy to reach the top level.

exam_phrases: use a ruler with smaller / millimetre divisions
add more weights (to increase the range)
move the ruler closer to the spring

mistakes.right: More accurate is ignored on its own. Say a ruler with smaller or millimetre divisions.

mistakes.wrong: Read the ruler at eye level to avoid parallax.
mistakes.right: Eye level or no parallax is ignored here. Move the ruler closer to the spring or use a pointer.

mistakes.wrong: See how much the rubber extends when another weight is added.
mistakes.right: This vague statement is ignored. Measure a length with a named device, such as a ruler, and calculate the extension as the difference between two lengths.

worked_example.question: A spring stands on a table. Weights are added to the spring and its length is measured with a ruler. State two ways that the experimental procedure could be improved.
answer_points: Any two from: use a ruler with millimetre divisions.
Add more weights to increase the range.
Move the ruler closer to the spring.
worked_example.tip: Any two improvements score one mark each. The answer must be specific.
